newsitem.title: UK: Nomura says involved in UK Co-op takeover scheme.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says involved in UK Co-op takeover scheme.

text.p: Nomura International said on Tuesday it was involved in a billion pound ($1.6 billion) plus bid to buy Britain's mutually-owned Co-operative Wholesale Society by entrepreneur Andrew Regan's specially formed Galileo Group.

"Nomura confirms it was preparing to complete legal formalities to provide Galileo with debt financing to support its proposals for the CWS," a Nomura spokesman told Reuters. The CWS has said it has no intention of selling any of its businesses, which range from supermarkets and funeral parlours to a bank, to Regan.

Last week CWS temporarily thwarted Galileo's ambitious plan to take over the 153-year-old group by court action against Regan, his Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica and Galileo, which has the backing of several City institutions.

Galileo had been ready to announce a proposal to convert the CWS into a limited company which it would then offer to buy. Banking sources said Nomura's role would involve providing a 1.2 billion pound debt facility to Galileo to support the bid rather than any equity stake in the firm.

The Nomura spokesman declined to give any further details of its involvement. However banking sources said the London-based arm of the huge Japanese securities house would continue to support the bid team if legal obstacles are removed.

While Regan and the others named in last week's High Court order gained an 18-hour extension on Tuesday, the legal process is not expected to end before the end of this week, making the details of the bid -- widely believed to be for between 1.0 and 1.5 billion pounds -- unlikely to surface in the near future. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
